title: Mid-Atlantic Buffer Rehearsal — ops notes and action items
content:
Context:
This doc captures the notes from the Mid-Atlantic buffer rehearsal on 2026-11-18 (0900–1030 PT). Objective was to run a scaled priming sequence against the mid-atlantic region, validate backfill behavior, and exercise the fast-fallback policy to Dedicated when edge slots saturate. This is not the final runbook — capturing rough observations and action items for the capacity & ops sprint.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner) — ops lead
- Marco Ruiz — fleet allocator
- Ellen Zhao — SRE / tracing
- Priya Narang — serving runtime
- Samir Kapoor — release engineering
- Observers: two solutions engineers (shadow)

Agenda:
1) Quick status and baseline metrics (5m)
2) Priming sequence: warm 120 mid-atlantic slots (30G mixed) over 15 minutes (20m)
3) Simulate a sudden regional traffic spike + capacity reclaim (20m)
4) Validate fallback to dedicated pool (10m)
5) Post-run telemetry check & open issues (15m)

Baseline before run:
- Allocated mid-atlantic capacity: 420 slots (mix of 10g/30g/40g)
- Idle buffer configured: 8% (target for region: 6–10%)
- Active prefix cache hit rate: 14% (global avg 17%)
- Median p50 token latency (mid-atlantic): 85ms; p95: 210ms
- Recent anomaly: small increase in eviction churn on 30g machines overnight (investigating)

What we ran (sequence):
- Step 1: Controlled warm-up (0–60 slots in 8 minutes) with 512-token synthetic prompts to populate KV caches
- Step 2: Rapid fill (60–120 slots) in next 7 minutes; concurrently triggered background batch jobs across the region to exercise scheduler
- Step 3: Induced preemption on 20% of 30g nodes (simulate host reclaim), then observed slot reallocation
- Step 4: Triggered fast-fallback policy rule: if reallocation latency > 90s AND routed-qps > 2500, route new sessions to Dedicated pool (tested with feature flag)

Observations (what surprised us):
- Cache priming effectiveness varied by model: smaller models (<=7B) reached 30–35% prefix hit after warm-up; larger models (~70B) saw <8% — implies priming needs model-aware sampling.
- Eviction churn spike correlated with concurrent background batch job scheduling — scheduler currently treats priming as same priority as model finetune jobs. Need priority tagging.
- Reallocation latency median was 48s, p95 173s — two factors contributed: (a) slow node initialization on a subset of older 30g hosts, (b) controller retrying allocations against constrained pools.
- Fast-fallback routed ~12% of new sessions to Dedicated during the induced reclaim; routing decisions respected customer routing policy but we saw a transient cost delta (rough calc: +18% token cost for affected sessions).
- Tracing shows increased RPC error 503 on the feeder service during the rapid fill window — likely due to bursting of request fanout to the balancer.

Telemetry / logs to review (followups):
- Ellen: trace ids for 2026-11-18T16:14Z–16:23Z (balancer fanout window) — collect and annotate.
- Marco: scheduler logs for priming jobs tagged as non-priority between 16:10–16:30 — propose a priority whitelist.
- Priya: model-specific priming effectiveness matrix (collect sampling distributions used during warm-up).

Action items (owners + due dates):
1) Priority-tag priming jobs in scheduler prototype (Marco) — due 2026-11-23.
2) Short-term: increase mid-atlantic idle buffer to 12% for next 72 hours to stabilize p95 latency (Aisha) — enact by 11/19 02:00 UTC.
3) Investigate older 30g host initialization path and produce a mitigation plan; check image boot profiling (Samir + infra) — due 2026-11-25.
4) Port fast-fallback cost telemetry into cost-explorer for per-customer breakdown (Finance + Observability) — Priya to own instrumentation; initial dashboard stub by 2026-11-24.
5) Tracing deep-dive and RPC 503 root cause (Ellen) — notes & preliminary RCA by 2026-11-20.
6) Add model-aware priming sample selector to Serving Runtime experiment branch (Priya) — experimental PR by 2026-11-30.
7) Add an alert for reallocation p95 > 150s (SRE) — create pager policy and escalation path (Ellen) by 2026-11-21.

Decisions made during run:
- Short-term buffer bump to 12% for 72 hours (see action item #2). Rationale: reduce user-visible latencies while we fix scheduler priority.
- Approved priority-tag prototype for priming jobs (Marco to implement).
- No change to fallback thresholds today; we'll rerun rehearsal after priority-tagging is in place.

Risks & open questions:
- Cost exposure from repeated fallback events during frequent regional noise — need to quantify ragged cost vs user impact tradeoffs.
- Will increasing idle buffer materially affect slot availability for bursty workloads in adjacent regions? (cross-region impact analysis needed).
- Does the scheduler priority change create starvation for low-priority background workloads that teams rely on? Need temporary compensation window or quotas.

Small capacity sketch (quick numbers used in decisions):
- Region total slots: 420
- Normal idle buffer 8% => idle ~34 slots
- Increased buffer 12% => idle ~50 slots (delta +16 slots)
- Priming target for rehearsal: 120 slots (approx 29% of region active capacity)

Follow-up test plan (short):
- Re-run rehearsal w/priority tagging enabled and the same priming cadence; measure reallocation p95 and RPC 503 incidence. Aim to reduce p95 reallocation < 120s. (Owner: Marco + Ellen)
- Run a model-mix priming test (weighted by 7B/13B/70B mix representative of real traffic) and measure cache hit rate by model. (Owner: Priya)
- Run cost-simulation for fallback routing using 48h traffic window; measure per-customer cost delta and identify thresholds for auto-rollbacks. (Owner: Finance/Observability)

Notes to self / informal observations (scratchpad):
- Need a small README in the priming job repo that describes recommended sampling strategies per model size — this keeps oncall from copy-pasting the same tiny-prompt workload.
- Consider short lived 'prefill' waves vs continuous low-rate priming; waves appear to be more effective for small-medium models from today's data.
- Remember: communicate buffer bump to sales/customer success for customers on Dedicated with strict cost SLAs (avoid surprise).

Appendix — quick references used in run:
- Feature flag used: ff/fast-fallback-midatlantic-2026-11 (toggle in ops console)
- Test customers routed for rehearse: cs-team-staging1, cs-team-staging2 (internal test tenants)
- Resource tracker snapshot id: rt-20261118-1630

If you have additional fragments or logs to drop, append them here and tag the action owner. We'll merge into the working runbook before the next rehearsal.

— Aisha
